amendments.body: Blocking: the diff only changes `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/tests/budget_tracking.rs:283`, `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/tests/budget_tracking.rs:412`, and `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/tests/budget_tracking.rs:441`. None of the provenance touch points called out by tanksim-6e5.7.1 (`crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs`, `crates/tank_data/src/lib.rs`, data/docs) are modified, and none of the required provenance roundtrip/validation/display tests were added. As submitted, this branch leaves the requested schema/loader/display feature unimplemented and the bead’s acceptance criteria unmet.
amendments.rationale: The patch is unrelated to the feature request, so merging it would not deliver the promised provenance capability.

amendments.body: `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/tests/budget_tracking.rs:287`, `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/tests/budget_tracking.rs:303`, and `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/tests/budget_tracking.rs:441` hard-code the current animal cohort names (`adult`, `sub_adult`, `juvenile`) and only treat flat `animal.*_count` names as future fields. A new nested cohort following the current schema, such as `animal.larvae.count` or `animal.larvae.reserve_g`, would no longer be auto-discovered by the structural coverage test, so the budget component arrays could drift out of sync without this guard failing.
amendments.rationale: This weakens the regression test that is supposed to catch new budget-bearing animal pools by convention.

payload.summary: Reviewed the only changed file plus the relevant budget/biology implementation and ran `cargo test -p tank_core --test budget_tracking` successfully. I found two blocking issues: the patch does not implement the provenance feature described in tanksim-6e5.7.1, and the rewritten budget-path helper now hard-codes current animal cohorts in a way that weakens future-field coverage.
